title: Stripe vs Paddle: Direct Payments, Merchant of Record and Billing
description: Compare Stripe Checkout, optional Stripe Managed Payments and Paddle's merchant-of-record model. Evaluate tax responsibility, supported products, subscriptions, checkout, disputes, fees and migration. Historical PilotStack winner is provisional, not a verified head-to-head result.

features.name: Primary business model
features.tool1: Direct payment processing, with a separate merchant-of-record option
features.tool2: Merchant of record for eligible digital-product sales
features.tool1Detail: Stripe Checkout supports hosted or embedded checkout for standard direct payments. Stripe Managed Payments is a distinct merchant-of-record service for eligible digital businesses; these are not the same contractual model. Official: https://stripe.com/payments/checkout and https://stripe.com/managed-payments
features.tool2Detail: Paddle documents that it acts as the reseller and merchant of record for supported digital-product transactions. Verify seller eligibility, product restrictions, buyer countries and terms. Official: https://www.paddle.com/about/procurement

features.name: Indirect tax responsibility
features.tool1: Depends on whether direct Stripe Payments or Managed Payments is used
features.tool2: Paddle handles sales-tax collection and remittance within its MoR scope
features.tool1Detail: For ordinary Stripe payments, the business generally retains tax responsibilities even if using Stripe Tax services. Stripe Managed Payments assumes specified indirect-tax responsibilities in supported markets. Confirm scope and legal terms. Official: https://stripe.com/managed-payments
features.tool2Detail: Paddle describes collecting and remitting applicable sales tax, VAT or GST when it is merchant of record. Sellers must still evaluate their other accounting and tax obligations. Official: https://www.paddle.com/help/start/intro-to-paddle/how-paddle-is-able-to-take-on-your-vat-and-tax-responsibilities

features.name: Checkout integration
features.tool1: Stripe-hosted or embedded Checkout, plus other payment interfaces
features.tool2: Paddle Checkout for eligible digital goods
features.tool1Detail: Pilot a representative purchase with a successful payment, failed payment, refund, and customer return. Confirm payment methods, currency, country, branding and webhooks for the selected integration. Official: https://stripe.com/payments/checkout
features.tool2Detail: Pilot the same scenarios using Paddle's current checkout and transaction lifecycle. Confirm merchant-of-record disclosure, tax display, localization and subscription support. Official: https://www.paddle.com/billing/checkout

features.name: Subscriptions and renewals
features.tool1: Stripe Billing for recurring revenue; confirm required paid add-ons
features.tool1Detail: Test subscription creation, initial payment failure, renewal failure, cancellation, retry policy, and accurate entitlement updates. Billing and Checkout may have distinct prices or requirements. Official: https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview
features.tool2Detail: Test subscription renewals, notifications, cancellations, refunds and customer billing support in Paddle. Confirm settlement timing and data export. Official: https://www.paddle.com/pricing

features.name: Business and regional eligibility
features.tool1: Direct Stripe accounts and Managed Payments have different regional/product requirements
features.tool2: MoR availability also depends on business, product, and region
features.tool1Detail: Confirm that the specific legal entity may open a standard Stripe account and whether Managed Payments is eligible for the product and intended markets. Official: https://stripe.com/global and https://stripe.com/managed-payments
features.tool2Detail: Confirm supplier eligibility, restricted product categories, supported payment origins and settlement arrangements with Paddle before migration. Official: https://www.paddle.com/about/procurement

features.name: Fees and total cost
features.tool1: Processing and additional products require a plan-specific calculation
features.tool2: MoR checkout and optional services follow Paddle's current terms
features.tool1Detail: Model country-specific processing, optional Billing or tax services, Managed Payments if selected, disputes, refunds, FX, and payout costs. Do not apply one advertised rate globally. Source: https://stripe.com/payments/checkout
features.tool2Detail: Model the MoR checkout charge, low-price transactions, refunds, FX, add-ons, and any custom terms. Compare like-for-like responsibilities, not just processing percentages. Source: https://www.paddle.com/pricing

features.name: Refunds, disputes and buyer support
features.tool1: Responsibility depends on standard processing versus Managed Payments
features.tool2: Merchant-of-record services include buyer transaction support within scope
features.tool1Detail: For direct payments, map who handles disputes, payment failure and customer communication. Managed Payments includes a different responsibility split. Confirm product and regional scope. Source: https://stripe.com/managed-payments
features.tool2Detail: Paddle's procurement page distinguishes its order-related support from the software supplier's product support. Map refunds, chargebacks and customer entitlement responsibilities. Source: https://www.paddle.com/about/procurement

features.name: Developer operations and webhooks
features.tool1: Test idempotency, webhook retries, order-to-payment records and reconciliation
features.tool2: Test event mapping, subscriptions, seller payouts and reconciliation
features.tool1Detail: Ensure a successful checkout redirect is not mistakenly treated as final payment confirmation. Test webhook replay, duplicate events and internal order reconciliation. Reference: https://docs.stripe.com/payments
features.tool2Detail: Test transaction and subscription state mapping, refunds, reconciliation exports and failure recovery. Verify the current developer documentation and API quotas: https://developer.paddle.com/

features.name: Migration and accounting
features.tool1: Export and validate payment, customer and subscription data
features.tool2: Confirm customer, billing and entitlement migration path
features.tool1Detail: Create a migration plan for subscriptions and stored payment methods, including customer consent and an approved approach to moving sensitive payment data. Verify relevant product limitations. Reference: https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview
features.tool2Detail: Confirm which existing subscriptions, customer data and payment credentials can move to Paddle under current vendor policies. Trial a representative migration, reconcile balances, and define rollback. Reference: https://www.paddle.com/pricing

features.name: Decision framework
features.tool1: Consider direct payments or optional MoR for supported use cases
features.tool2: Consider bundled MoR for eligible digital commerce
features.tool1Detail: Start with the desired seller-of-record and tax-responsibility arrangement, then test payment and accounting workflows. Stripe Managed Payments may change the comparison for eligible businesses. Official: https://stripe.com/managed-payments
features.tool2Detail: Assess whether Paddle's MoR scope and product restrictions match your business, then compare operational effort, contract terms and total fees. Official: https://www.paddle.com/help/sell/tax/how-paddle-handles-vat-on-your-behalf

verdict: Stripe and Paddle overlap in accepting payments for digital businesses, but the key decision is the commercial and operational model, not a fabricated universal score. Standard Stripe Checkout lets eligible businesses take direct payments while retaining relevant seller responsibilities; Stripe also offers an optional Managed Payments merchant-of-record service for supported digital products and markets. Paddle positions its checkout and billing as a merchant-of-record arrangement for eligible digital sales. Choose by seller eligibility, responsibility for tax and buyer support, subscription and refund operations, developer integration, payout reconciliation and written total cost. PilotStack's stored Stripe pick is a provisional legacy editorial record, not an independently benchmarked result. Run the same payment, failed renewal, refund and export scenarios before choosing.

faqs.question: Is Stripe only a payment processor while Paddle is a merchant of record?
faqs.answer: No. Standard Stripe payments operate differently from Paddle's merchant-of-record offering, but Stripe also has Managed Payments as a separate merchant-of-record product for eligible digital businesses. Confirm the responsibility split and product eligibility directly: https://stripe.com/managed-payments and https://www.paddle.com/about/procurement.

faqs.question: Does choosing Paddle remove every tax obligation for a business?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Paddle describes assuming indirect-tax collection and remittance for supported merchant-of-record transactions. The software supplier may still have other accounting, income-tax, invoicing and reporting duties. Check the written agreement, markets, and your qualified adviser: https://www.paddle.com/help/start/intro-to-paddle/how-paddle-is-able-to-take-on-your-vat-and-tax-responsibilities.

faqs.question: How should I compare the cost of Stripe and Paddle?
faqs.answer: Use identical transaction amounts, volumes, currencies and refund scenarios, and specify whether Stripe's Managed Payments, Billing, Tax or other products are included. Compare the services and responsibilities included in the quote rather than dividing unrelated headline fees. Sources: https://stripe.com/payments/checkout and https://www.paddle.com/pricing.

faqs.question: What should a subscription SaaS business test before switching?
faqs.answer: Test sign-up, first-payment failure, recurring invoice, renewal failure, cancel/reactivate, refund, entitlement update, duplicate webhook delivery, exports and bookkeeping reconciliation. Confirm which customer or subscription records can be migrated, and who is responsible for customer communications.

faqs.question: Does PilotStack have a verified head-to-head winner?
faqs.answer: No. A historical Stripe pick and recorded editorial ratings exist in the source dataset but are not independently validated as a controlled comparison. Treat the recorded pick as provisional; the recommended choice depends on your specific business and payment responsibilities.
